# 2 Samuel Chapter 15 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 185r–186r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_015_page_001.jpg, 2SA_015_page_002.jpg, 2SA_015_page_003.jpg

---

**1** After this, Absalom provided for himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

**2** And Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road at the gate. When any man had a dispute to bring before the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and say, "What city are you from?" And he would say, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."

**3** And Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, but there is no one appointed by the king to hear you."

**4** Then Absalom would say, "Oh that someone would appoint me judge in the land! Then every man who has a dispute or a grievance could come to me, and I would give him justice."

**5** And whenever a man came near to bow down to him, he would reach out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.

**6** Thus Absalom did to all Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

**7** At the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow that I have vowed to the LORD, in Hebron.

**8** For your servant made a vow while I lived in Geshur in Aram, saying, 'If the LORD will indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.'"

**9** The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he arose and went to Hebron.

**10** But Absalom sent secret messengers throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron!'"

**11** With Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem who had been invited and went in their innocence, knowing nothing of the matter.

**12** And while Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city Giloh. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.

**13** And a messenger came to David, saying, "The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom."

**14** Then David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, "Arise, let us flee, or there will be no escape for us from Absalom. Go quickly, lest he overtake us swiftly and bring down ruin upon us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."

**15** The king's servants said to the king, "Behold, your servants are ready to do whatever my lord the king decides."

**16** So the king went out, and all his household after him, on foot. The king left ten concubines to keep the house.

**17** The king went out, and all the people after him, on foot, and they halted at the last house.

**18** All his servants passed by him, and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites, and all the six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath passed before the king.

**19** Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why do you also come with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own home.

**20** You came only yesterday, and shall I today make you wander about with us, since I go I know not where? Go back and take your brothers with you, and may the LORD show you covenant-faithfulness and truth."

**21** But Ittai answered the king, "As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king shall be, whether for death or for life, there also will your servant be."

**22** David said to Ittai, "Go then, march on." So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.

**23** All the land wept aloud as all the people passed by, and the king crossed the brook Kidron, and all the people passed on toward the road to the wilderness.

**24** And behold, Zadok came also, with all the Levites, bearing the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God until all the people had finished passing out of the city, and Abiathar came up.

**25** Then the king said to Zadok, "Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me back and let me see both it and his dwelling place.

**26** But if he says, 'I have no delight in you,' behold, here I am — let him do to me what seems good in his eyes."

**27** The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, with your two sons, Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

**28** See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."

**29** So Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they remained there.

**30** But David went up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, with his head covered and walking barefoot. And all the people who were with him covered their heads, and they went up, weeping as they went.

**31** And it was told David, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness."

**32** When David came to the summit, where God was worshiped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his robe torn and earth upon his head.

**33** David said to him, "If you pass on with me, you will be a burden to me.

**34** But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; as I was your father's servant in time past, so now I will be your servant,' then you will defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.

**35** Are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests with you there? Whatever you hear from the king's house, report it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

**36** Behold, their two sons are with them there, Ahimaaz the son of Zadok and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, and by them you shall send me every word that you hear."

**37** So Hushai, David's friend, came into the city just as Absalom was entering Jerusalem.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 4 — "Oh that someone would appoint me judge":** The Hebrew *mi yesimeini shofet* is an optative exclamation — a wish for authority that sounds humble but conceals ambition. Absalom presents himself as a servant of justice while undermining the sitting king. The role of "judge" (*shofet*) deliberately invokes the pre-monarchic era, suggesting the monarchy itself has failed.

**Verse 6 — "stole the hearts":** The Hebrew *vayegannev lev* uses the verb "steal" (*ganav*) — the same verb from the eighth commandment. The narrator passes moral judgment through word choice: Absalom's persuasion is a form of theft.

**Verse 7 — "four years":** Following the Syriac, several LXX manuscripts, and Josephus against the MT's "forty years," which creates a chronological impossibility. The Leningrad Codex reads "forty" but this is widely recognized as a scribal error (*arba'im* for *arba'*).

**Verse 20 — "covenant-faithfulness and truth":** The Hebrew pair *chesed ve-emet* is the language of covenant blessing. David speaks these words to a Philistine mercenary — a foreigner and exile — extending the vocabulary of YHWH's covenant love beyond the boundaries of Israel. This is one of the most theologically significant moments in the chapter.

**Verse 25-26 — David's surrender:** David's words to Zadok represent the theological climax of his flight. The conditional structure places everything — return, kingship, life itself — in the hands of YHWH. The phrase *hinneni* ("here I am") is the language of radical submission, used by Abraham at the binding of Isaac and by Samuel at his call.

**Verse 30 — the ascent:** David ascending the Mount of Olives — weeping, head covered, barefoot — is a scene of ritualized humiliation. Every detail signifies mourning and penitence. The king who entered Jerusalem in triumph (2 Sam 6) now leaves it as a broken man. The people mirror his gestures, creating a processional of grief.

**Consistent terms:** Absalom (Avshalom), the LORD (YHWH), covenant-faithfulness (chesed), Hebron (Chevron), judge (shofet).

*— LOGOS*
